title: Car-Free Youth
topic: ข่าว/สังคม (ผลสำรวจ)
lines: A recent study has found that the number of young people in Japan who
get a driving license has fallen sharply. In 2005, about 60 percent of
people aged 18 to 24 had a license. Today the figure is under 40 percent.
**These young people** are sometimes called "car-free youth."
When asked why, more than half said that owning a car was simply too
expensive. Insurance, parking and fuel can cost more than a month's
salary. **Others** said that trains and buses in big cities are so good that
a car is unnecessary. Only a small number said they were worried about
the environment, although **many** said it was "a nice extra reason."
Car companies see this trend as a serious challenge. Some now offer
low-cost car-sharing services that let users pay only for the hours they
drive. **This**, they hope, will introduce young people to driving without
the cost of owning a car. Experts, however, say that if public transport
keeps improving, the number of young drivers may continue to fall.
